# filterfdr tutorial

Filtering out genes before testing (by fold change, variance or average signal) is meant to soften the
multiple-testing correction and raise power. van Iterson, Boer and Menezes showed that a filter biases the
FDR when it removes null features unevenly across the p-value range, and proposed a permutation test for
that bias. This package rebuilds their methods: the simulation, the filters, achieved FDR and power after
filtering, the FDR-bias test, and the p-value densities after filtering.

> van Iterson M, Boer JM, Menezes RX. Filtering, FDR and power. *BMC Bioinformatics* 11:450 (2010).
> [doi:10.1186/1471-2105-11-450](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-11-450)

```{r setup, include = FALSE, dev = "pdf"}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", dev = "pdf")
```

## Install

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jeonglab-bcm/fossil/PMC2949886/package")
```

```{r load}
library(filterfdr)
packageVersion("filterfdr")
```

## Example input

1000 simulated features, 10 samples per group, 20% of them differentially expressed (the paper's design;
the `null` column holds the truth).

```{r input}
d <- read_two_group(example_path("example_data.csv"))
dim(d$x)
table(d$group)
table(null = d$null)
round(d$x[1:3, c(1:3, 11:13)], 3)
```

## Run the method

Remove 0, 25, 50 or 75% of the features with each filter, correct the p-values of the rest with
Benjamini-Hochberg at 5%, and score the result against the truth.

```{r run}
res <- filter_curve(d, fractions = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75), methods = "BH")
res[, c("filter", "fraction", "kept", "rejected", "fdr", "power")]
```

```{r table}
reshape(res[, c("filter", "fraction", "fdr")], idvar = "fraction", timevar = "filter", direction = "wide")
```

The fold-change filter raises both the power and the achieved FDR; the signal and variance filters do not.

## Compare with the expected output

`expected_fdr_power.csv` was computed with base R alone (`t.test`, `quantile`, `p.adjust`).

```{r compare}
ref <- read.csv(example_path("expected_fdr_power.csv"))
m <- merge(ref, res, by = c("filter", "fraction"), suffixes = c(".expected", ".ours"))
ok <- m$rejected.expected == m$rejected.ours & abs(m$fdr.expected - m$fdr.ours) < 1e-12 &
  abs(m$power.expected - m$power.ours) < 1e-12
cat(sum(ok), "of", nrow(m), "rows match the expected output\n")
stopifnot(all(ok))
```

The p-value densities after filtering (the paper's Fig. 1, t test with 8 degrees of freedom, 25% removed)
against the values read from the authors' original figure:

```{r density}
pub <- read.csv(example_path("fig1_published.csv"))
pub$ours <- mapply(function(p, h, f) pvalue_density_filtered(p, nu = 8, delta = if (h == "null") 0 else 1,
                                                             filter = f, removed = 0.25),
                   pub$p, pub$hypothesis, pub$filter)
cat(sum(abs(pub$ours - pub$density) < 0.01), "of", nrow(pub), "published density values within 0.01\n")
stopifnot(all(abs(pub$ours - pub$density) < 0.01))
head(pub)
```

## Test a filter for FDR bias

Permute the samples of each feature independently, filter, and test whether the p-values left in are
still uniform; repeat and test the per-permutation p-values against U[0, 1]. More permutations (the paper
uses 1000) give a sharper test.

```{r biastest}
set.seed(42)
fc <- fdr_bias_test(d$x, d$group, filter = "foldchange", fractions = c(0, 0.1, 0.5), nperm = 100)
sg <- fdr_bias_test(d$x, d$group, filter = "signal", fractions = c(0, 0.1, 0.5), nperm = 100)
data.frame(fraction = c(0, 0.1, 0.5), foldchange = fc$label, signal = sg$label)
```

`***` marks p < 0.001. On this small example the test flags the fold-change filter at 50% removed and
leaves the signal filter alone. With the paper's 5000 features and 1000 permutations it flags the
fold-change filter already at 10% removed (see the reproduction).

## Your own data

- `read_two_group()` reads a CSV with a `feature` column and one column per sample named by group and
  number (`X1, X2, ..., Y1, Y2, ...`), on a log scale. A logical `null` column is needed only to score
  achieved FDR and power, which requires knowing the truth (simulations).
- `fdr_bias_test(x, group, filter, fractions, nperm)` needs no truth: run it on your data with the filter
  and fractions you plan to use. `filter` is `"foldchange"`, `"signal"` or `"variance"`. Each column of
  `Q` holds the per-permutation p-values; `p.value` is the test of the filter at that fraction.
- `filter_curve()` methods: `"BH"`, `"BY"`, `"aBH"` (multtest's two-stage procedure), `"qvalue"`;
  `test = "wilcoxon"` uses the rank-sum test.
- `simulate_two_group()` generates data with the paper's design.
